references.text: Before this verse, John describes that Jesus wept, which triggers the Jews' comment about his love. Weeping and love are directly linked in this sequence.
Here the author explicitly confirms that Jesus loved Lazarus, which is the direct reason for the Jews' observation in verse 36 that he loved him.
Jesus is described as deeply moved and troubled in his own soul just before he weeps, leading to the Jews' conclusion about his strong love.
This verse summarizes Jesus' entire life and death by stating that he loved his own who were in the world, which forms the theological background for the specific love shown to Lazarus.
